key_insight: High task completion did not ensure appropriate withholding: browser agents often submitted sequencing prior authorizations despite designed deficiencies.
clinical_relevance: Automating exome/genome sequencing prior authorization could reduce administrative burden, but unreliable withholding raises concerns about unsupervised use.
method: Built a simulated payer portal and synthetic EHR containing 836 compliant or deliberately deficient patient profiles.
Evaluated Gemini 3 Pro, Gemini 3 Flash, and Claude Opus 4.5 for task completion, form accuracy, and appropriate withholding.
Ran two replication experiments on 100 profiles to assess run-to-run variability.
evidence_signal: Initial task completion ranged from 56.1% to 95.5%, while correct withholding on deficient profiles ranged from 0% to 17.3%; only 18.0–48.0% of tasks had identical outcomes across three runs.
watch_item: Synthetic sandbox results do not establish real-world safety; submission bias and run-to-run variability warrant human oversight before deployment.
paper_title: Hard to Halt: Automation Bias in Agent-Driven Sequencing Prior Authorization Workflows
